content.title: Bill Self addresses his future as Kansas head coach following seasonending loss
content.text: The Kansas head coach discussed his future after the end of his 23rd season. SAN DIEGO — Shortly after Kansas basketball's season-ending loss to St. John's on Sunday afternoon, Bill Self said he will go home and discuss his coaching future with his family.Just a few weeks ago, Self said he would only continue to coach if he felt good. Now, with his 23rd season as head coach officially over, he was asked if this season was his last."I'll get back and get with family and visit and see what's going on," Self said. "I love what I do. I need to be able to do it where I'm feeling good and healthy to do it fairly well. I'll get back home and it will all be discussed."Self's comments came with Kansas AD Travis Goff standing some 20 feet away from the podium. Should the 2025-26 campaign be his last, Goff would be tasked with hiring the ninth head coach in program history.But, has Self made up his mind at this point?"No, I haven't decided," Self said. "I'll get back and visit with family. I've had, obviously, some issues off the court health-wise. And that will be discussed. But I love what I do. I want to feel good while I'm doing it, though. We'll get back and we'll discuss that when we get back."Last summer, Self was taken to Lawrence Memorial Hospital on July 24 after he experienced what KU described at the time as "concerning symptoms." Self had two stents put in at the time. The procedure in July was the latest measure health professionals have taken to help Self. Back in March of 2023, Self had two stents put in after he had chest tightness prior to the start of the Big 12 Tournament in Kansas City. The procedure kept Self out of the 2023 postseason. In previous interviews discussing his health, Self has mentioned that he underwent an aortic valve replacement in the fall of 2022, following KU's national championship season.Self missed one game this season due to a health-related issue. He was taken to the hospital in January. Self later said he was dehydrated and had AFib. He did not travel to KU's game against Colorado but returned to the bench a few days later when KU played K-State.Health wise, Self was asked if he's healthy. "I feel as good as I've felt in a long time," Self said. "I'm not making any statements whatsoever. But every year, I think -- it used to be you work -- when you get to be doing it as long as I've done it, I look at it in five-year increments. Now I'm probably looking at it in more two-year increments, so to speak. So I try to focus on this season and try to get us to a second weekend, which we failed at. So I'll go back now and break it down and see where that leads."Everything Bill Self said after KU's loss to St. John'sThe KU head coach discussed the loss, what happened down the stretch and what's next.SAN DIEGO — A buzzer-beater from St. John's guard Dylan Darling ended Kansas' season on Sunday afternoon. The Jayhawks fell to the Red Storm 67-65 in the Round of 32. KU battled back from 14 points down to tie the game with 13 seconds to play. But KU was unable to get the final defensive stop to force overtime.As a team, KU shot 44% from the field while St. John's shot 36% from the field. The Jayhawks made five 3s compared to the 11 from the Red Storm, which was their most since Jan. 10. Individually, Darryn Peterson led KU with 21 points and four rebounds. Melvin Council Jr. recorded 15 points, nine rebounds and four assists while Flory Bidunga scored 12 point with five rebounds.Postgame, Bill Self met with reporters to discuss the game. Here's everything the KU coach said postgame…Self began with an opening statement…"Well, the tournament is, one of the things that makes it so great is that it can be great, but it can also be cruel. We obviously put ourselves in a position to play from behind the whole game, and then really competed and played great down the stretch and just didn't finish what we had started down the stretch. But certainly disappointed, sad for our guys, because they tried so hard. But just a tough afternoon."On Flory Bidunga getting in foul trouble and what KU changed to match St. John's…"We really didn't change. We put Paul in. Actually, I thought Paul played great. I thought he played big. They kicked us on the glass to start the game. Couple of them were, we got our butts whipped, but a couple of them were kind of unfortunate bounces, too. But I thought defensively for the entire game we played the scout report. We didn't want Hopkins to shoot set shots, but he's averaging -- I think he's made, what, 20 on the year, something like that, .6 a game. We would probably live with that for the most part. I wish we would have bluffed at him a couple of times. But he just made shots that basically our scouting report said if he takes them, he takes them."On Kohl Rosario and his impact down the stretch… "Well, yeah, we tried to get our best defensive team in there. So that was why we did that. Obviously it wasn't a very good effort on us the last, what was it, 3.9? We had to guard four bounces, and we didn't guard four bounces. Yeah, that was really disappointing. But Kohl did a great job. That's hard not to play and then be inserted in and do what he did in a short amount of time. I thought he was great." On his coaching future, what he's gone through and what his plan is… "I haven't really gone through much on the court. I've gone through some stuff off the court. So I'll get back and get with family and visit and see what's going on. I love what I do. I need to be able to do it where I'm feeling good and healthy to do it fairly well. I'll get back home and it will all be discussed." On the physical side of the game and how his team matched up… "I thought great after the start of the game. I thought the first five to seven minutes we didn't, and then after that I thought we did very well. Zuby made the two plays late. Catches the ball in the dead corner with 3 on the shot clock, drives it and shoots a right-hand jump hook and scores. And then he makes the really good spin move late. Other than that, I thought, until the last play, I thought we defended them soundly. We rebounded it well. We offensive rebounded. They were playing a little bit like we were on Friday, just trying to get to the finish line. And we were more aggressive. And I wish we'd been that way earlier in the game." On KU's fouling at the end of the game and the goal… "Use the clock, that's what I was thinking. I wish that when Kohl fouled the first time, he fouled in one second. I wish he could have just let him hold it and foul with five seconds into it. So now you've got a situation where maybe there's not 3.9. Maybe there's 2.0 or 1.5. But our whole deal was, with only two team fouls, why wouldn't you go ahead and foul in that situation? We left them too much time. But irregardless of that, gotta guard three or four bounces, and we didn't do it." On his future at KU and if he's made a decision… "No, I haven't decided. I'll get back and visit with family. I've had obviously some issues off the court health-wise. And that will be discussed. But I love what I do. I want to feel good while I'm doing it, though. We'll get back and we'll discuss that when we get back." On the team and if it ever got the rhythm he wanted… "I didn't think we ever got rhythm offensively the whole year. It's one thing to get rhythm, but it's another thing, when you go against teams like Houston and Arizona and St. John's that guard differently than the other teams guard you. So it is easier to get rhythm when you're comfortable. And the key to having rhythm is doing it when you're put under duress. And I didn't think we handled that very well at all. At the end, we were aggressive and play to athletic ability and went and made athletic plays, which was great. But certainly a -- frustrating year would be probably too much to say. But it's certainly a year that didn't seem like it was nothing about it was very smooth. Seemed like, to me, we were having to adjust on the fly quite a bit." On Darryn Peterson and his performance… "I thought he played well. I thought he played really hard. The thing about it is, when you guard as well and as hard as what St. John's does, those shots are hard shots. And you switch coming off every screen and all that stuff. Those are hard plays. I thought he competed hard. I was really proud of his effort. He's had moments where he's looked great and moments where obviously his health didn't allow him to play like we all know he's capable of playing. But I hope the year was enjoyable for him. I know I enjoyed being around him an awful lot." On his health, how he's feeling, if he's had anything go on and if he's completely healthy… "I don't know about completely. But I'm feeling -- I feel as good as I've felt in a long time. I'm not making any statements whatsoever. But every year, I think -- it used to be you work -- when you get to be doing it as long as I've done it, I look at it in five-year increments. Now I'm probably looking at it in more two-year increments, so to speak. So I try to focus on this season and try to get us to a second weekend, which we failed at. So I'll go back now and break it down and see where that leads." On not making the second weekend again and what needs to change… "You're right, the first year we were a 1 seed, and I had serious health issues and I didn't finish the season. The last two years hasn't been -- well this year included -- it's been inconsistent and not as good. So obviously it's disappointing. I really feel that we had a team this year that could have been a higher seed if we would have played better in other games. And if you're a higher seed, you don't play St. John's in the second game, arguably the hottest team in the tournament. But a new identity, no, no. That's not it. I actually believe that we need to do a really good job evaluating and recruiting." On the team and how proud he is of them… "I think they hung in there, through the ups and the downs. I thought they hung in there and stayed together and played hard for the most part all year long. I thought they competed hard. The thing about this group, as you guys saw, our margin for error offensively isn't that great. So you've got to be really good and competitive defensively in rebounding the ball. When we did that, we could make other teams play poorly to the point where that was enough. We actually did that fairly well tonight, but obviously, Hopkins made 6. We didn't score the ball or take care of the ball in a manner in which you need to to beat a team like St. John's." On the buzzer beater and if it'd be a terrible way for his career to end… "Yeah, you missed my point earlier. My career ain't going to be based on one game. Whatever. I said I was going to get back and evaluate my health situation. So I think you kind of missed the point on that one." On KU's roster building and recruiting… "Well, you know, you're going to have to figure out who's staying, who's not staying, portal. I just think in today's time, the next four to six weeks will be indicative to the question that was asked earlier is, how can you improve yourself moving forward? The next four to six weeks will be the most important time to do that."Three observations from KU's 67-65 loss to St. John'sBreaking down KU's performance.SAN DIEGO — Kansas fell to St. John's 67-65 on Sunday. The Jayhawks fell at the buzzer due to a made layup from Dylan Darling, which ended KU's season.Here are three observations from the game…KU had nothing going offensively in the first halfThe Jayhawks have had some major struggles offensively to close the season. KU went into the Round of 32 shooting 39.8% from the field over the last 10 games. That ranks 353rd nationally.KU had struggles down the stretch against Cal Baptist, with someone not named Darryn Peterson making just one basket over the final 10 minutes of the contest. The game on Sunday started in a similar fashion, with Peterson knocking down two 3s. A teammate didn't make a shot from the field in the first half until Elmarko Jackson's transition dunk at the 10:19 mark of the first half. Put another away, in almost a half of basketball KU got two make field goals from someone besides Peterson.KU got some better play in the middle of the first half, with several players chipping in. But, it was a slow start offensively that put KU behind the eight ball.At the half, KU was shooting 34.5% from the field. The Jayhawks posted just 26 points in the opening frame and had almost as many turnovers (9) as made field goals (10).Two starters struggled to make an impact, while two freshmen provided good minutes off the bench Bill Self issued a challenge to his starting wings and big men prior to the game, they needed to play tough, be aggressive and get 50/50 balls.Starters Tre White and Bryson Tiller struggled to make a consistent impact in the game. Tiller finished the game scoreless and White didn't make his first basket until the 3:16 mark of the second half. The two combined to go 2 for 8 from the field with three turnovers.On the glass, White grabbed five rebounds and Tiller grabbed five rebounds in their combined 54 minutes on the floor.Off the bench. Paul Mbiya gave Self some good minutes in the first half. He got some run in the second half but foul trouble kept him on the bench. The big man grabbed six rebounds and scored four points in his 13 minutes.Late in the game, Self turned to freshman Kohl Rosario, who didn't play in the first round game. He knocked down a 3 from the corner and then grabbed a defensive rebound. With 2:41 to play, Rosario grabbed an offensive rebound and put it back in to make it a three point game.It was a positive performance to end the season for the two freshmen, while starters White and Tiller had their own struggles.KU crashes out of the NCAA Tournament at a familiar spotKU has now made one Sweet 16 in its last seven NCAA Tournaments. For the fifth time during that stretch, KU has lost in the Round of 32.Sunday evening's game had a different feel than past Round of 32 exits. Instead of wilting when the Jayhawks got dow by 14 points in the second half, the Jayhawks battled back. They showed grit during their run to tie the game.KU competed, got stops, created extra possessions and made tough shots, certainly traits that weren't always prevalent in its performance. But, as Self said postgame, KU needed to guard for 3.9 seconds and it didn't.As a result, KU has missed the Sweet 16 again. Now, a big offseason is officially underway.
